question.problem: Given the curve $r(t)=({t}^{2}-2)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j,$ $t\in (0,\infty )$, find all of the points at which ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $r(t)$ are perpendicular.
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})\,j \\  & =2t\,i+2t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ [({t}^{2}-2)\,i+{t}^{2}\,j]\cdot (2t\,i+2t\,j) & =0 \\ ({t}^{2}-2)\cdot 2t+{t}^{2}\cdot 2t & =0 \\ 2t(2{t}^{2}-2) & =0 \\ 4t({t}^{2}-1) & =0 \\ 4t(t-1)(t+1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =((1)^{2}-2)\,i+(1)^{2}\,j=-\,i+j,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $r(t)$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(-1,1).$
